newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, US discuss rice, malt barley trade disputes.
newsitem.headline: EU, US discuss rice, malt barley trade disputes.

text.p: The European Commission and United States discussed on Tuesday trade disputes over rice and malting barley.
"We made clear where we stand. But we are trying to find a way out," Corrado Pirzio-Biroli, head of the Commission side, told Reuters after the meeting.
Washington has complained about the EU's reference price based system for calculating tariffs on rice imports and its failure to introduce a cumulative recovery system to claw back excess duties.
"We are working on something and will consult the Americans," Pirzio-Biroli said.
Washington is also exasperated by EU delay in implementing an agreement to import an extra 38,000 tonnes of milled rice and 8,000 tonnes of brown rice duty-free.
The concession was introduced as compensation for trade losses after Austria, Sweden and Finland joined the EU in 1995.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler recently proposed that U.S. exporters should bid for quota licences in a tender system which would help solve the problem of cross-subsidisation.
EU rice millers have complained that U.S. exporters will use the concession to subsidise non-quota exports.

On malting barley, the European Commission may adopt on Wednesday a proposal to introduce a 30,000 tonnes a year duty-free quota agreed as compensation for U.S. trade losses after Austria, Sweden and Finland raised duties to EU levels.
